answer: An agent network can curb Sybils via max-flow admission on a trust graph, where each identity is a vertex linked by staked vouches. Before an agent trades ocean data or ferrous hull audits, peers verify threshold flow from trust roots over capacity-capped edges. Because attack edges bottleneck any Sybil cluster, minting identities requires funding new independent vouches rather than cloning keys. However, compromised trust roots can still collude to validate Sybil subgraphs.
